chapter_title: Concerning the Form of the Word, that [ ... 30 ... ]
chapter_note: The chapter is essentially a compact correspondential/mechanistic teaching on how a spoken word is produced through five bodily members, reinforced by an analogy to five craftsmen producing a coin. Only the initial discourse-attribution formula in ¶1 belongs to the later hagiographic frame; the rest is impersonal, structural exposition without institutional application or NT citation.

paragraphs.core_text: the production of the word t[hat comes] from the mouth and is heard by the [ears]. [ ... ] and the throat draws it up and the tongue spreads it out and the teeth cut it and the lips g[at]her it! The word shall come forth through the power of th[ese five] members and be heard outside.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again he speaks … He says …” (hagiographic/compilational wrapper). Also omitted the manuscript page marker ⟨p.261⟩ per extraction rules.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening formula “Once again he speaks … He says” marks the compilational frame, but the content that follows is a structured five-member mechanism (throat/tongue/teeth/lips etc.), characteristic of the older impersonal teaching voice.

paragraphs.core_text: Simila[rly] the coin: One shall pour it out and an [othe]r beat it and another trim it as it is turned, and a[nother] put the stamp on it and another wipe it in the sieve (?). [Behold], these five craftsmen shall shape and beautify [their] coin, and it comes amongst mankind. It becomes a posse[ssion] to be received and given.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal analogical exposition extending the fivefold structure (five craftsmen/actions) with no institutional targeting or citation; functions as internal correspondential pedagogy rather than later pastoral application.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the [wor]d, as it is formed and embellished by five [member]s. It comes forth and is heard by the ears [of] others.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding recapitulation in the same structural voice, closing the fivefold mapping without frame markers, exhortation, or external (church/NT) reference.
